guide_enrichment.narrative:
Our numbers are slightly more favorable toward Syracuse than the market, largely because we see enough stability in the passing game to keep the offense competitive. Steve Angeli returned from his 2025 season-ending injury and threw for 263 yards in the opener, while Umari Hatcher produced career highs of eight catches, 147 yards and two touchdowns. We also saw Syracuse's offensive line earn an 87.0 pass-blocking grade from PFF. Those results came against New Hampshire, so we are treating them as encouraging context rather than proof against a much stronger opponent.

The concern for us is whether Syracuse can prevent Louisville from controlling the game on the ground. Our longer-run metrics give Louisville a substantial advantage in rushing efficiency, and that could create repeated scoring opportunities while limiting Syracuse's possessions. Syracuse held New Hampshire to 60 rushing yards, but one opener does not erase the broader concern. We can see a path for Syracuse to remain competitive through Angeli and the passing game, but the price does not give us enough separation from our expectation to make this a wager.
guide_enrichment.matchup_to_watch: For us, Louisville's rushing offense against Syracuse's run defense is the matchup that can determine whether the underdog stays within range. If Louisville consistently generates efficient runs, Syracuse could be forced to defend long drives while its offense plays from less favorable game states. We saw Syracuse's rebuilt front produce five sacks in the opener—one-quarter of its entire 2025 total—but run defense is the more important test here, and our numbers still make it the clearest pressure point.

recent_game.fact: Syracuse opened the 2026 season with a 66-3 home win over New Hampshire.
Syracuse scored 41 first-half points and finished with 513 total yards, including 238 rushing and 275 passing.
The defense held New Hampshire to three points and 159 total yards while recording five sacks and nine tackles for loss.
Syracuse committed no turnovers and gained three takeaways against New Hampshire.
Syracuse used 84 players against New Hampshire, including 45 freshmen or sophomores.

quarterback.fact: Steve Angeli returned from the season-ending injury he suffered against Clemson in 2025 and passed for 263 yards against New Hampshire.
Angeli's New Hampshire performance extended his streak of games with at least 230 passing yards to six; he has thrown for at least 245 yards in each of his five Syracuse appearances.
Angeli had two passes graded as big-time throws and no turnover-worthy plays against New Hampshire, according to PFF.
Angeli entered 2026 with 176 completions in 265 attempts for 2,352 yards, 23 touchdowns and three interceptions across Syracuse and Notre Dame.
Amari Odom, a January 2026 transfer, threw his first Syracuse touchdown pass against New Hampshire after earning First Team All-Conference USA honors in 2025.

offensive_personnel.fact: True freshman Shavane Anderson Jr. rushed 10 times for 102 yards and three touchdowns in his collegiate debut against New Hampshire.
Tylik Hill made his first career start and rushed 16 times for 91 yards and his first collegiate touchdown against New Hampshire.
Umari Hatcher returned after missing the 2025 season because of injury and set career highs with eight catches, 147 yards and two touchdowns against New Hampshire.
Transfer running back Ahmad Miller led the SWAC with 1,054 rushing yards and nine touchdowns in 2025 at Jackson State.
Running back Ju'Juan Johnson transferred from LSU in spring 2026 after recording 48 carries for 169 yards and two touchdowns there.
Tight end David Clement recorded career highs of two catches and 35 yards and scored his first collegiate touchdown against New Hampshire.
Oluwafunto Akinshilo, a spring 2026 transfer, made his first career start at guard against New Hampshire.
The projected offensive line was Trevion Mack at left tackle, Oluwafunto Akinshilo at left guard, Joe Cruz at center, Byron Washington at right guard and Kam Pringle at right tackle.
Syracuse's offensive line received an 87.0 pass-blocking grade from PFF against New Hampshire, second best among ACC teams through that Saturday's games.
Center Joe Cruz had appeared in 38 games with 17 starts and had allowed one sack in 657 career pass-blocking opportunities, according to PFF.
Right guard Byron Washington allowed no pressures against New Hampshire, while right tackle Kam Pringle allowed one pressure, according to PFF.

defensive_personnel.fact: Four of Syracuse's five sacks against New Hampshire were recorded by transfers.
Transfer edge defender Keyshawn Johnson recorded 2.5 sacks, four tackles and a forced fumble in his Syracuse debut.
Transfer defensive lineman Tunmise Adeleye tied his career high with six tackles and recorded a sack in his Syracuse debut.
Transfer defensive lineman Jartavius Flounoy had four tackles, a half-tackle for loss and a forced fumble in his Syracuse debut.
Defensive lineman Rashard Perry returned after a season-ending 2025 injury and recorded three tackles and his first career interception against New Hampshire.
Cornerback Chris Peal allowed 14 receiving yards when targeted and led Syracuse with four solo tackles against New Hampshire, according to PFF.
Demetres Samuel Jr. entered 2026 with nine pass breakups and one interception from his freshman season, tying for the most passes defended among returning ACC defensive backs.
